sentence: The originals were acceptable. Scanning every receipt added no benefit.
setupText: Choose the formulation that itself presents scanning as already performed but unnecessary.
taskText: The originals were acceptable. Scanning every receipt added no benefit.
text: Choose the formulation that itself presents scanning as already performed but unnecessary. The originals were acceptable. Scanning every receipt added no benefit.
options: The receipts did not need to be scanned.
The receipts should have been scanned.
The receipts must not have been scanned.
The receipts needn't have been scanned.
answer: The receipts needn't have been scanned.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2361:Unnecessary completed action versus absence of requirement
explanation: Needn't have been scanned normally presents an action that was performed although unnecessary, matching the stated wasted effort.

Did not need to removes a requirement but does not itself say whether scanning happened.
Needn't have been scanned normally presents an action that was performed although unnecessary, matching the stated wasted effort.
Should have been scanned presents scanning as desirable or required, reversing the judgment of unnecessary work.
Must not have been scanned suggests a deduction that scanning did not occur, not that it occurred unnecessarily.

sentence: The investigation has not established whether the access code was shared.
setupText: Choose the cautious statement preserving lack of knowledge rather than asserting non-disclosure.
taskText: The investigation has not established whether the access code was shared.
text: Choose the cautious statement preserving lack of knowledge rather than asserting non-disclosure. The investigation has not established whether the access code was shared.
options: The code is known not to have been shared.
The code is known to have been kept private.
The code is not known to have been shared.
The code is believed to have remained private.
answer: The code is not known to have been shared.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2362:Negation scope in a reporting passive
explanation: Not known to have been shared withholds knowledge of sharing while leaving open whether sharing occurred.

rationales.The code is known not to have been share: Known not to asserts established non-sharing, which the investigation has not established.
rationales.The code is known to have been kept priv: Known to have been kept private also claims knowledge of non-disclosure.
rationales.The code is not known to have been share: Not known to have been shared withholds knowledge of sharing while leaving open whether sharing occurred.
rationales.The code is believed to have remained pr: This substitutes a positive belief in privacy for the stated absence of an established outcome.

sentence: The adviser resented ___.
setupText: Choose the continuation saying the committee had overruled the adviser, which she resented.
taskText: The adviser resented ___.
text: Choose the continuation saying the committee had overruled the adviser, which she resented. The adviser resented ___.
options: having overruled the committee
not having overruled the committee
not having been overruled by the committee
having been overruled by the committee
answer: having been overruled by the committee
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2363:Perfect passive gerund with preserved agent and polarity
explanation: Having been overruled gives the adviser the receiver role and places the committee's earlier action inside the object of her resentment.

rationales.having overruled the committee: The active perfect gerund makes the adviser the person who overruled the committee.
rationales.not having overruled the committee: This makes her resent failing to overrule the committee, changing both role and polarity.
rationales.not having been overruled by the committ: This makes her resent the absence of an overruling, whereas she resents the overruling that occurred.
rationales.having been overruled by the committee: Having been overruled gives the adviser the receiver role and places the committee's earlier action inside the object of her resentment.

sentence: When the observatory reopened, the dome was thought to have been reinforced.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that keeps the reported belief separate from verified work.
taskText: When the observatory reopened, the dome was thought to have been reinforced.
text: Choose the interpretation that keeps the reported belief separate from verified work. When the observatory reopened, the dome was thought to have been reinforced.
options: People then believed earlier reinforcement had occurred; the sentence does not verify it.
People now believe reinforcement had occurred before an earlier, unspecified belief.
The sentence verifies earlier reinforcement but attributes its purpose to the reopening.
People then considered earlier reinforcement necessary; the sentence leaves its occurrence open.
answer: People then believed earlier reinforcement had occurred; the sentence does not verify it.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2364:Past reporting frame with earlier unverified passive content
explanation: Was thought anchors the belief at the past reopening, while to have been reinforced places the supposed work earlier without verifying it.

rationales.People then believed earlier reinforceme: Was thought anchors the belief at the past reopening, while to have been reinforced places the supposed work earlier without verifying it.
rationales.People now believe reinforcement had occ: The finite 'was thought' locates the belief in the past; it does not report a belief held now.
rationales.The sentence verifies earlier reinforcem: The content of thought is the supposed reinforcement itself, not just its purpose.
rationales.People then considered earlier reinforce: Thought to have been reinforced reports a belief about occurrence, not a judgment that reinforcement was necessary.

sentence: The firm employed only local workers for the restoration.
setupText: Choose the passive paraphrase preserving the scope of 'only' over the workers employed.
taskText: The firm employed only local workers for the restoration.
text: Choose the passive paraphrase preserving the scope of 'only' over the workers employed. The firm employed only local workers for the restoration.
options: Only local workers were employed by the firm for the restoration.
Local workers were employed only by the firm for the restoration.
Local workers were employed by the firm only for the restoration.
Only the firm employed local workers for the restoration.
answer: Only local workers were employed by the firm for the restoration.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2365:Focus-particle scope preserved across a passive paraphrase
explanation: 'Only local workers' keeps the restriction on which workers the firm employed.

rationales.Local workers were employed only by the: 'Only by the firm' excludes other employers, not nonlocal workers.
rationales.Only local workers were employed by the: 'Only local workers' keeps the restriction on which workers the firm employed.
rationales.Local workers were employed by the firm: 'Only for the restoration' limits the work's purpose or occasion rather than the workers' locality.
rationales.Only the firm employed local workers for: 'Only the firm' restricts the employer and is active, changing the original scope.

sentence: The pumps need inspecting, and the engineers insist on inspecting them personally.
setupText: Choose the interpretation assigning the inspecting role correctly in both clauses.
taskText: The pumps need inspecting, and the engineers insist on inspecting them personally.
text: Choose the interpretation assigning the inspecting role correctly in both clauses. The pumps need inspecting, and the engineers insist on inspecting them personally.
options: The pumps perform the first inspection, and the engineers perform the second.
The pumps are to receive inspection, and the engineers intend to perform it.
Both -ing forms make their preceding subjects the receivers of inspection.
The first clause describes inspection already completed; the second describes inspection still required.
answer: The pumps are to receive inspection, and the engineers intend to perform it.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2366:Passive meaning after need versus active gerund after insist
explanation: 'Need inspecting' means 'need to be inspected', whereas the active complement of 'insist' assigns the inspecting to the engineers.

rationales.The pumps perform the first inspection,: Need inspecting has a passive meaning here: the pumps need someone to inspect them.
rationales.Both -ing forms make their preceding sub: After insist on, inspecting is active and the engineers are its understood actors.
rationales.The first clause describes inspection al: 'Need' expresses a requirement, not a completed inspection; neither '-ing' ending alone determines completion.
rationales.The pumps are to receive inspection, and: 'Need inspecting' means 'need to be inspected', whereas the active complement of 'insist' assigns the inspecting to the engineers.

sentence: It remains to be seen whether the new timetable will reduce crowding.
setupText: Choose the interpretation preserving the uncertainty expressed by the passive idiom.
taskText: It remains to be seen whether the new timetable will reduce crowding.
text: Choose the interpretation preserving the uncertainty expressed by the passive idiom. It remains to be seen whether the new timetable will reduce crowding.
options: The effect on crowding has not yet been established.
The effect has been established but has not yet been announced.
The timetable has already been observed reducing crowding.
An observer must watch every journey before the timetable can be introduced.
answer: The effect on crowding has not yet been established.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2367:Unresolved outcome in remains to be seen
explanation: Remains to be seen presents the outcome as still unresolved, rather than reporting an observation already made.

rationales.The effect on crowding has not yet been: Remains to be seen presents the outcome as still unresolved, rather than reporting an observation already made.
rationales.The effect has been established but has: The idiom concerns unresolved knowledge, not merely delayed publication of known results.
rationales.The timetable has already been observed: This asserts an observed benefit that the sentence leaves open.
rationales.An observer must watch every journey bef: The expression does not impose a literal observation procedure or a condition for introducing the timetable.

sentence: A: 'I have three candidates to interview.' B: 'I have three candidates to be interviewed.'
setupText: Choose the comparison that does not invent a different interviewer.
taskText: A: 'I have three candidates to interview.' B: 'I have three candidates to be interviewed.'
text: Choose the comparison that does not invent a different interviewer. A: 'I have three candidates to interview.' B: 'I have three candidates to be interviewed.'
options: B requires someone other than the speaker to conduct the interviews.
B leaves the interviewer unexpressed; the speaker may still conduct them.
A says the interviews are complete, while B says they are pending.
B makes the candidates the people who will interview the speaker.
answer: B leaves the interviewer unexpressed; the speaker may still conduct them.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2368:Unexpressed agent in a noun-modifying passive infinitive
explanation: To be interviewed places the candidates as receivers and leaves the interviewer unspecified, which does not rule the speaker out.

rationales.B requires someone other than the speake: The passive leaves the actor unexpressed; it does not require the actor to differ from the speaker.
rationales.A says the interviews are complete, whil: The infinitives in both versions can refer to pending interviews, not completed ones.
rationales.B leaves the interviewer unexpressed; th: To be interviewed places the candidates as receivers and leaves the interviewer unspecified, which does not rule the speaker out.
rationales.B makes the candidates the people who wi: The candidates receive interviewing in B; they do not become the interviewers.

sentence: A witness watched the visitor for a few seconds midway across the courtyard.
setupText: Choose the report explicitly presenting the observed activity from within, without presenting the crossing as a whole or an inference.
taskText: A witness watched the visitor for a few seconds midway across the courtyard.
text: Choose the report explicitly presenting the observed activity from within, without presenting the crossing as a whole or an inference. A witness watched the visitor for a few seconds midway across the courtyard.
options: The visitor was seen crossing the courtyard.
The visitor was seen to have crossed the courtyard.
The visitor was seen to cross the courtyard.
The visitor was understood to have been crossing the courtyard.
answer: The visitor was seen crossing the courtyard.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2369:Progressive versus whole-event complement of passive perception
explanation: Was seen crossing places the directly observed visitor within the unfolding activity without claiming observation of the whole crossing.

rationales.The visitor was seen to have crossed the: To have crossed presents a crossing as anterior to the perception or evidential judgment, not as the activity directly observed from within.
rationales.The visitor was seen crossing the courty: Was seen crossing places the directly observed visitor within the unfolding activity without claiming observation of the whole crossing.
rationales.The visitor was seen to cross the courty: Was seen to cross presents the crossing as an observed whole event, stronger than the limited view described.
rationales.The visitor was understood to have been: Was understood to have been crossing reports an understanding about an earlier activity, not the witness's direct visual observation.

sentence: A: 'We had our roof repaired.' B: 'We had repaired our roof.'
setupText: Choose the comparison appropriate to a context in which a family hired roofers.
taskText: A: 'We had our roof repaired.' B: 'We had repaired our roof.'
text: Choose the comparison appropriate to a context in which a family hired roofers. A: 'We had our roof repaired.' B: 'We had repaired our roof.'
options: A and B both identify the family as the people who physically carried out the repairs.
A describes arranging a service; B makes 'we' the repairers in an active past-perfect clause.
A reports an earlier completed repair by the family, while B reports hiring roofers.
A is past perfect, while B is an ordinary past passive.
answer: A describes arranging a service; B makes 'we' the repairers in an active past-perfect clause.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2370:Causative have versus perfect have distinguished by object placement
explanation: The position of our roof distinguishes the service construction from the active perfect; the given context selects the arranged-service reading for A.

rationales.A and B both identify the family as the: In the supplied hiring context, A presents the family as arranging the service, not physically carrying out the repair.
rationales.A reports an earlier completed repair by: This reverses the causative-service reading of A and the active perfect structure of B.
rationales.A is past perfect, while B is an ordinar: A has causative 'had' plus object plus participle; B has the perfect auxiliary 'had' immediately before 'repaired'.
rationales.A describes arranging a service; B makes: The position of our roof distinguishes the service construction from the active perfect; the given context selects the arranged-service reading for A.

sentence: The manuscript was said by its donor to have been translated by a local scholar.
setupText: Choose the role assignment that preserves attribution without verifying the attributed event.
taskText: The manuscript was said by its donor to have been translated by a local scholar.
text: Choose the role assignment that preserves attribution without verifying the attributed event. The manuscript was said by its donor to have been translated by a local scholar.
options: The donor is the translator; the scholar supplies the claim.
Both donor and scholar are identified as sources making the same claim.
The donor supplies the claim, and the sentence independently verifies the scholar's translation.
The donor supplies the claim; the scholar is its alleged translator.
answer: The donor supplies the claim; the scholar is its alleged translator.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2371:Agent attachment across nested reporting and event passives
explanation: By its donor attaches to was said; by a local scholar attaches to translated inside the reported claim.

rationales.The donor supplies the claim; the schola: By its donor attaches to was said; by a local scholar attaches to translated inside the reported claim.
rationales.The donor is the translator; the scholar: This reverses the two by phrases' attachments to different passive verbs.
rationales.Both donor and scholar are identified as: The scholar is described as performing translation, not as making a statement.
rationales.The donor supplies the claim, and the se: Was said attributes the translation claim to the donor; it does not independently verify its content.

sentence: A: 'The route was considered safe.' B: 'The route was considered to be safe.'
setupText: Choose the comparison that respects the status of a reported assessment.
taskText: A: 'The route was considered safe.' B: 'The route was considered to be safe.'
text: Choose the comparison that respects the status of a reported assessment. A: 'The route was considered safe.' B: 'The route was considered to be safe.'
options: A states proven safety; B reports only an assessment.
A describes past safety; B predicts safety after the assessment.
To be makes B an instruction to make the route safe rather than an assessment.
Both report an assessment of safety, without independently verifying safety.
answer: Both report an assessment of safety, without independently verifying safety.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2372:Adjective complement versus to-be complement after a passive judgment verb
explanation: Both complements are available after 'was considered' here. Neither construction by itself makes the reported judgment an independently established fact.

rationales.A states proven safety; B reports only a: Omitting to be does not turn considered into an assertion of proven safety.
rationales.A describes past safety; B predicts safe: To be need not place safety later; both can describe the assessment of a state at the same time.
rationales.Both report an assessment of safety, wit: Both complements are available after 'was considered' here. Neither construction by itself makes the reported judgment an independently established fact.
rationales.To be makes B an instruction to make the: To be is part of the complement describing the assessed state, not an instruction to change the route.

sentence: The records show a mixture of screened and unscreened passengers.
setupText: Choose the statement unambiguously preserving that some passengers were screened and some were not.
taskText: The records show a mixture of screened and unscreened passengers.
text: Choose the statement unambiguously preserving that some passengers were screened and some were not. The records show a mixture of screened and unscreened passengers.
options: All the passengers were not screened before boarding.
None of the passengers were screened before boarding.
Some, but not all, passengers were screened before boarding.
No passengers were left unscreened before boarding.
answer: Some, but not all, passengers were screened before boarding.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2373:Quantifier-negation scope in a passive coverage statement
explanation: Some, but not all explicitly preserves both a screened group and an unscreened group.

rationales.All the passengers were not screened bef: All ... not can be read with different scope in usage; it does not unambiguously state the required mixture.
rationales.Some, but not all, passengers were scree: Some, but not all explicitly preserves both a screened group and an unscreened group.
rationales.None of the passengers were screened bef: None denies screening for the whole group, losing the screened passengers.
rationales.No passengers were left unscreened befor: No passengers left unscreened says everyone was screened, losing the unscreened group.

sentence: No agreement was arrived at during mediation.
setupText: Choose the analysis explaining why this passive is possible without treating all uses of 'arrive' as transitive.
taskText: No agreement was arrived at during mediation.
text: Choose the analysis explaining why this passive is possible without treating all uses of 'arrive' as transitive. No agreement was arrived at during mediation.
options: The preposition 'at' is an optional location phrase, so 'agreement' is a direct object promoted to subject.
The unit 'arrive at' means reach a conclusion; 'agreement' is promoted from its prepositional complement.
The passive construction adds an agreement as an object to the otherwise unchanged physical-arrival sense.
The preposition supplies the omitted agent, so no agreement identifies the people who failed to arrive.
answer: The unit 'arrive at' means reach a conclusion; 'agreement' is promoted from its prepositional complement.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2374:Figurative prepositional passive versus literal intransitive arrive
explanation: The figurative prepositional construction licenses 'agreement' as a passive subject. This does not make ordinary intransitive physical 'arrive' generally passivizable.

rationales.The preposition 'at' is an optional loca: 'At' is part of the figurative 'arrive at' construction here, not an optional location phrase after a direct object.
rationales.The passive construction adds an agreeme: The acceptability depends on the figurative prepositional construction, not on passivization creating a direct object for physical 'arrive'.
rationales.The preposition supplies the omitted age: 'At' does not introduce an agent here; agreement identifies the outcome that was not reached.
rationales.The unit 'arrive at' means reach a concl: The figurative prepositional construction licenses 'agreement' as a passive subject. This does not make ordinary intransitive physical 'arrive' generally passivizable.

sentence: A manual says, 'The hatch is supposed to be sealed during testing.' An unverified recollection says, 'The hatch is supposed to have been sealed before the trial.'
setupText: Choose the comparison matching the stated sources of the two sentences.
taskText: A manual says, 'The hatch is supposed to be sealed during testing.' An unverified recollection says, 'The hatch is supposed to have been sealed before the trial.'
text: Choose the comparison matching the stated sources of the two sentences. A manual says, 'The hatch is supposed to be sealed during testing.' An unverified recollection says, 'The hatch is supposed to have been sealed before the trial.'
options: Both sentences independently confirm that the hatch was sealed as required.
A attributes an earlier belief; B gives an instruction for a future trial.
A gives a requirement; B attributes an unverified belief about earlier sealing.
Both sentences describe an action currently being performed on the hatch.
answer: A gives a requirement; B attributes an unverified belief about earlier sealing.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2375:Obligation versus report in be supposed to constructions
explanation: The manual context selects an obligation reading; the recollection context and perfect infinitive select an attributed earlier-event reading.

rationales.A gives a requirement; B attributes an u: The manual context selects an obligation reading; the recollection context and perfect infinitive select an attributed earlier-event reading.
rationales.Both sentences independently confirm tha: Neither an instruction nor an unverified recollection independently establishes that sealing occurred.
rationales.A attributes an earlier belief; B gives: This reverses the contexts and overlooks the perfect infinitive in the recollection.
rationales.Both sentences describe an action curren: Neither be sealed nor have been sealed is the progressive being sealed, and the sources concern a rule and an earlier event.

sentence: Staff weighed the samples. The samples then dried on their own.
setupText: Choose the sentence explicitly making weighing passive and subsequent natural drying active.
taskText: Staff weighed the samples. The samples then dried on their own.
text: Choose the sentence explicitly making weighing passive and subsequent natural drying active. Staff weighed the samples. The samples then dried on their own.
options: The samples were weighed and were dried afterward.
The samples were weighed; they then dried naturally.
The samples were weighed and dried afterward.
Staff weighed the samples and dried them afterward.
answer: The samples were weighed; they then dried naturally.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2376:Auxiliary scope in coordination with an intransitive change
explanation: Were weighed makes the measurement passive, while they dried is an active intransitive clause describing the natural change.

rationales.The samples were weighed and were dried: Repeating were marks drying as passive rather than the explicitly active natural process requested.
rationales.The samples were weighed and dried after: The shared were allows dried to be read as a coordinated passive; it does not make the natural active reading explicit.
rationales.The samples were weighed; they then drie: Were weighed makes the measurement passive, while they dried is an active intransitive clause describing the natural change.
rationales.Staff weighed the samples and dried them: This keeps weighing active and makes staff the agents of drying, rather than preserving the requested voice contrast.

sentence: The residents objected to the bridge being demolished without their being consulted.
setupText: Choose the analysis preserving the two affected parties without assuming that demolition has already occurred.
taskText: The residents objected to the bridge being demolished without their being consulted.
text: Choose the analysis preserving the two affected parties without assuming that demolition has already occurred. The residents objected to the bridge being demolished without their being consulted.
options: The objection concerns demolition of the bridge without consultation of the residents; it may concern a proposed action.
The residents oppose being made responsible for demolition without first approving the plan.
The residents object to a completed demolition, and both passive gerunds independently establish completed events.
The residents oppose consultation about the bridge unless demolition has first been completed.
answer: The objection concerns demolition of the bridge without consultation of the residents; it may concern a proposed action.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2377:Distinct subjects in nested passive gerund clauses
explanation: The bridge is the subject of being demolished, and their refers to the residents as potential consultees; the gerunds do not by themselves establish completed events.

rationales.The residents oppose being made responsi: The residents are the potential recipients of consultation, not the stated demolition workers.
rationales.The objection concerns demolition of the: The bridge is the subject of being demolished, and their refers to the residents as potential consultees; the gerunds do not by themselves establish completed events.
rationales.The residents object to a completed demo: Neither passive gerund contains a perfect marking, and an objection can concern a proposal rather than something already done.
rationales.The residents oppose consultation about: Without places the absence of consultation within the objection; it does not make completed demolition a condition for consultation.

sentence: The customs inspection prevented the artifacts from being exported.
setupText: Choose the passive recast preserving successful prevention, not merely an attempt or a rule.
taskText: The customs inspection prevented the artifacts from being exported.
text: Choose the passive recast preserving successful prevention, not merely an attempt or a rule. The customs inspection prevented the artifacts from being exported.
options: The artifacts were subjected to an inspection intended to prevent their export.
The artifacts were not permitted to be exported following the customs inspection.
The artifacts were prevented by the customs inspection from being exported.
The artifacts were inspected to determine whether their export could be prevented.
answer: The artifacts were prevented by the customs inspection from being exported.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2378:Two passive layers within a prevention construction
explanation: The inspection remains the preventing cause, and export remains the event stopped from occurring.

rationales.The artifacts were subjected to an inspe: An inspection intended to prevent export states a purpose but does not establish that prevention succeeded.
rationales.The artifacts were not permitted to be e: A prohibition does not itself establish that export was prevented in practice.
rationales.The artifacts were inspected to determin: This substitutes an assessment of possible prevention for the stated successful prevention.
rationales.The artifacts were prevented by the cust: The inspection remains the preventing cause, and export remains the event stopped from occurring.

sentence: Participants were shown to recognize familiar melodies more quickly than unfamiliar ones.
setupText: Choose the interpretation of 'shown to' in this research statement.
taskText: Participants were shown to recognize familiar melodies more quickly than unfamiliar ones.
text: Choose the interpretation of 'shown to' in this research statement. Participants were shown to recognize familiar melodies more quickly than unfamiliar ones.
options: Participants were shown pictures telling them which melodies were familiar.
Researchers instructed participants to recognize familiar melodies more quickly.
Evidence demonstrated a difference in participants' recognition speed.
Participants demonstrated the melodies to the researchers.
answer: Evidence demonstrated a difference in participants' recognition speed.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2379:Evidential shown to versus literal presentation and instruction
explanation: 'Were shown to' introduces a finding established by evidence about the participants' behavior.

rationales.Evidence demonstrated a difference in pa: 'Were shown to' introduces a finding established by evidence about the participants' behavior.
rationales.Participants were shown pictures telling: 'Shown to recognize' is not the double-object construction in which people are shown pictures or other objects.
rationales.Researchers instructed participants to r: The sentence reports a demonstrated result, not an instruction to perform differently.
rationales.Participants demonstrated the melodies t: Participants are the subjects of 'recognize', not the people showing melodies to researchers.

sentence: The stadium has been being renovated by local contractors for months.
setupText: Choose the active recast preserving the continuing process, accumulated duration, and named workers without adding a completion claim.
taskText: The stadium has been being renovated by local contractors for months.
text: Choose the active recast preserving the continuing process, accumulated duration, and named workers without adding a completion claim. The stadium has been being renovated by local contractors for months.
options: Local contractors have had the stadium renovated for months.
Local contractors have had months in which to renovate the stadium.
Local contractors have renovated the stadium over a period of months.
Local contractors have been renovating the stadium for months.
answer: Local contractors have been renovating the stadium for months.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c1-2380:Active recast of a grammatical but cumbersome perfect progressive passive
explanation: The active perfect progressive preserves the ongoing duration and named actor while avoiding the cumbersome passive auxiliary sequence.

rationales.Local contractors have had the stadium r: Have had the stadium renovated presents a causative arrangement or resulting condition; it does not retain the contractors as the grammatical performers of an ongoing process.
rationales.Local contractors have had months in whi: Having time available does not assert that the contractors have actually been carrying out the work.
rationales.Local contractors have been renovating t: The active perfect progressive preserves the ongoing duration and named actor while avoiding the cumbersome passive auxiliary sequence.
rationales.Local contractors have renovated the sta: The simple perfect presents the renovation as an accomplished whole rather than retaining the original process viewpoint.
